Bach worked at the Thomaskirche in Leipzig; Handel staged operas in London. The two never met in their lives.
Mozart set up on his own in Vienna and died in 1791 at 35. The Requiem was left unfinished.
Paganini and Liszt sent Europe into a frenzy, and Chopin played in the salons of Paris. Paganini died in 1840.
Wagner opened his own theatre in Bayreuth, and Brahms brought out his First Symphony. Wagner died in 1883.
Mahler led the Vienna Court Opera, and died in 1911 leaving his Tenth Symphony unfinished.

What does music say?
Absolute music
Programme music
Music is complete in sound alone. To use it to explain stories and pictures is to degrade it, do you not think?
Only when joined to poetry and story does music open new worlds. Music that is nothing but form is out of date, do you not think?
The content of music is nothing other than forms set in motion in sound
the view of those who prized Classical form (later given its theory by the critic Hanslick)
the view the critic Hanslick set out in On the Musically Beautiful (1854)
Joined to poetry, music depicts what words cannot reach
the view Berlioz showed in the Symphonie fantastique (1830)
the view Liszt showed in the symphonic poem and Wagner in the music drama
Form and poetry are both wings of music
How to regard virtuosity
Service to the work
The performer is the composer's servant. To flaunt one's skill and carry off the applause is not art, I should say?
Transcendent technique that takes the audience's breath away is a performer's life. Anyone can simply play what is written, do you not think?
The performer is one who serves the work
the view of composers who honoured the notes on the page
the stance Gluck demanded in his reform of opera (drama and music before the singer's skill)
the stance Clara Schumann and Joachim held to throughout
Skill no one can imitate takes music to new places
the brilliant ornamented singing of castrati such as Farinelli
the path on which Clementi and the other keyboard virtuosos vied
the path opened by Paganini and Liszt
Skill exists to make the work shine
For whom does music exist?
For art
For the audience
Let those understand who can. To write to suit the public's taste is decadence, do you not think?
If the public takes no pleasure in it, what is music for? A piece that is merely difficult is the maker's self-indulgence, is it not?
Music aims at the heights without courting the listener
Bach wrote at the end of his scores: 'To the glory of God alone'
the stance of forebears such as J.S. Bach, who aimed at the heights of craft rather than fashion
the idea of 'art for art's sake', which spread in the 19th century
Music exists for those who listen
the stance Telemann and Handel showed through public concerts and enterprise
To satisfy connoisseur and layman alike is the real thing
Tradition or innovation?
Tradition
Innovation
Our forebears' rules have their reasons. To claim 'novelty' without having studied counterpoint or form is mere ignorance, is it not?
Rules exist to be broken. What sort of artist writes the same music as yesterday?
Only when the rules are known through and through is music free
the teaching handed down since Fux's counterpoint treatise Gradus ad Parnassum (1725)
If it pleases the ear, that is the new rule
the view Monteverdi showed in the 'second practice'
the view of C.P.E. Bach and the others of the 'sensitive style'
the view of Berlioz and Liszt
the 'music of the future' that Wagner proclaimed
a view attributed to Debussy ('pleasure is the rule')
On the foundation of tradition, one builds a new house
A nation's music, or a universal language?
A universal language
A nation's music
Music is a language that crosses frontiers. To cling to folk song and national character is narrow, do you not think?
Music born of our own folk songs and our own language is the real thing. What is gained by imitating other countries?
Music is a language understood by people of every country
the universality at which Viennese Classicism aimed
From the songs of the soil comes a music that belongs to that country alone
the view of the national schools: Smetana, Dvořák and others
Only what is rooted in its soil reaches the world
